name: The learner's own material becomes a skill outline
does: An uploaded PDF, Word file, text or paste is cut into passages; a model plans the course window by window (each window told the skills planned so far), in the material's own order, as units of skills: at most one skill per 250 characters and 30 in all. The model is told to merge neighbouring topics rather than stop early; the code keeps at most the window's share, so a model that returns more loses its last ones. Topics the material only names (a syllabus line) are marked and taught from general knowledge, labelled as such.

name: Placement over the skill graph skips what the learner already knows
does: One question at a time, the placement keeps a joint belief over which skills are known: each answer is read with the built-in placement answer model taken at its two ends (10% slips; guessing plus 15 points of luck); knowing a skill makes its prerequisites likely known; a shared rate of right answers ties untested skills together. The belief is sampled (Gibbs) and the next question is the one expected to shrink total uncertainty most: this graph belief and selection are new here, not the built-in one-dimensional walk. Every skill it would skip then gets a quick check (a miss earns a second question), like the built-in unit-skip check. Known skills are skipped and come back for review.

name: Spaced review timed to this learner's forgetting
does: A mastered skill falls due when its predicted recall drops to 75% on the half-life forgetting curve of the app's scorecard (its default curve, not the population fit), which grows with each right answer. Each review moves this learner's own half-life multiplier by a simple step (0.6 times how far the prediction missed), read against the learner's accuracy on skills they had just mastered so slips are not taken for forgetting. 2 of 2 right stretches the interval, 1 of 2 halves it (at least a day), 0 of 2 reopens the skill for remediation.
